Option B: “AI should guide students, not do the work for them.”

Option D: “Faculty should only use AI for administrative tasks, never for teaching.”
Correct answer: (Poll: no correct answer set in Curipod. Intended answer: B)

Question: A colleague says only a minority of students really use AI. In the Digital Education Council's 2024 global survey (3,839 students, 16 countries), what share used ChatGPT?
Explanation shown to students: ChatGPT is first in every survey that names tools. Grammarly and Copilot were 25% each, and 95% of UK undergraduates use AI in some form (HEPI 2026).

Question: Harvard's Faculty of Arts and Sciences gave students ChatGPT Edu, then ended open access after June 2026. Why?
Option C: A US ban on AI in coursework
Option D: It moved everyone to a local model
Explanation shown to students: Harvard cited cost and undergraduate uptake far lower than it expected. A licence alone doesn't change what students use.

Question: A strong student's essay gets a 68% AI score in Turnitin. Under HEC's August 2026 draft AI policy, what should you do first?
Option A: Read it, ask for drafts, talk to the student
Option B: Fail it: 68% is above any threshold
Option C: Confirm with two more free detectors
Option D: Ignore it: detectors are always wrong
Correct answer: Read it, ask for drafts, talk to the student
Explanation shown to students: HEC's draft says no penalty on an AI-detection report alone. It also asks every university for an AI policy and committee, student disclosure of AI use, and AI literacy within two years. Yale, Vanderbilt and Johns Hopkins switched Turnitin's AI detector off.

Question: VU Amsterdam does not license ChatGPT, and teachers there may not require students to use it. Why?
Option A: It costs too much per student
Option B: Dutch law bans AI in teaching
Option D: No data-processing agreement, which GDPR requires
Correct answer: No data-processing agreement, which GDPR requires
Explanation shown to students: Under GDPR (Article 28), a university that lets a supplier process personal data needs a contract with it. That's why European universities favour licensed tools or their own platforms.

Question: About 30 German universities used HAWKI in 2024, and Baden-Württemberg's bwGPT runs on it. What is HAWKI?
Option B: A self-hosted, open-source AI chat interface
Correct answer: A self-hosted, open-source AI chat interface
Explanation shown to students: First built at HAWK Hildesheim, it gives privacy-first access to AI models. Germany's data-protection rules push universities to shared or self-run platforms such as KI:connect.nrw, HAWKI and GWDG Chat AI.

Question: A colleague wants to stop students from simply pasting the assignment into ChatGPT. Which assessment design strategy is most aligned with current best practice?
Option A: Ban all AI tools and rely only on Turnitin’s AI score.
Option B: Make every assignment multiple-choice so AI cannot help.
Option C: Redesign the task so students must show process, oral defence, etc.
Correct answer: Redesign the task so students must show process, oral defence, etc.
Explanation shown to students: No vendor sees the data or trains on it (compare Brown's open models on HPC, GWDG's open models, ETH's Apertus). Trade-offs: local models are usually smaller and need hardware and staff.

Question: Your university wants to connect a third-party AI tutoring tool to Sakai so that student grades can flow back automatically and class rosters stay in sync. Which standard is the modern, more secure choice?
Explanation shown to students: LTI 1.3 replaces the shared key and secret with signed tokens, and a Sakai admin (CICT) registers the tool once. Until then: PPTX into Resources, questions into Tests & Quizzes.

Question: Recent 2025–2026 reports (WEF, LinkedIn, employer surveys) show a clear gap between what industry expects and what many university courses currently emphasise. The most accurate summary of that gap is:
Option A: Industry no longer values technical skills; only soft skills matter.
Option B: AI literacy and critical use of AI are essential skills for graduates.
Option C: Universities are already producing exactly the AI-ready graduates industry wants.
Option D: The only missing skill is coding in Python.
Correct answer: AI literacy and critical use of AI are essential skills for graduates.
Explanation shown to students: Write the questions as markup text, then use Tests & Quizzes > Create using markup text. We found no Sakai integration for Gemini Notebook, so check each output and move it in by hand.

Question: A student asks what IBA's rule on AI use is. Under HEC's August 2026 draft policy, where must IBA set out its AI rules?
Option D: An IBA AI policy, and every course outline
Correct answer: An IBA AI policy, and every course outline
Explanation shown to students: HEC's draft asks every university to write its own AI policy, set up an AI committee and report to HEC each year, and every course outline must state what AI use is allowed. We found no public IBA-wide AI policy yet (Oct 2026), so for now students should follow each course outline.

Question: Why is Gemini Notebook (formerly NotebookLM) better than a general chatbot for working from your own paper?
Option C: It answers from your uploads, with citations
Correct answer: It answers from your uploads, with citations
Explanation shown to students: It is grounded in your sources and cites them. Grounded doesn't mean correct: a citation can point to the right page and still misread it.
